subject: Pricing guidance during Hosted API experiment — enablement materials + rollout plan
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Chris Osei <chris.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Pricing guidance during Hosted API experiment — enablement materials + rollout plan

Hi Isabelle + Chris,

We’re getting increased AE/CSM questions on how to quote during the current Hosted API pricing experiments (credits + overage tiers + some plan gating). Right now the answers are scattered across Slack threads and older docs, and reps are mixing guidance.

Can we align on a single “approved talk track” and a short quoting decision tree for the experiment window?

What I think we need (drafts attached):
1) 1-pager: “How to quote while experiment is active” (eligibility rules, which pricebook to use, how to message variance vs old pricing).
2) FAQ: meter definitions + common edge cases (streaming tokens, retries, cached tokens, rounding).
3) Enablement deck: what changed, what didn’t, examples (console usage vs invoice), objections.

Proposed rollout plan:
- Fri EOD: content freeze + approvals (Sales Ops + Product Ops + Finance)
- Mon: publish in Confluence + pin in #sales and #customer-success
- Tue/Wed: 30-min live training + recording, then add to onboarding

Key open questions I need answered to finalize:
- Do discounts stack with free credits for experiment cohorts? (Some AEs are doing both.)
- If a customer is on an older contract rate card but is eligible for experiment pricing, do we (a) move them, (b) treat as net-new only, or (c) case-by-case with approvals?
- What’s the sanctioned explanation when console ≠ invoice by small amounts (time zone cutoffs, rounding, streaming partials)?

If you can each do a quick pass today, I can consolidate and send for approvals.

Attachments:
- Pricing_Change_Enablement_Deck_draft.pptx
- Pricing_Metering_FAQ_for_AEs_CSMs_draft_v0.3.docx
- Experiment_Quote_Guidance_OnePager_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference


From: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Chris Osei <chris.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 10:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Pricing guidance during Hosted API experiment — enablement materials + rollout plan

+1. We had 3 separate questions yesterday alone that were basically “which number do I put on the quote.”

From Sales Ops POV, we need:
- a single pricebook / SKU mapping for the experiment variants (even if the underlying experiment is more nuanced)
- a hard rule on stacking (discounts + credits + partner marketplace credits)
- escalation path: who can approve exceptions and what’s the paper trail (HubSpot note + approval email?)

Also: the 1-pager needs to explicitly call out “do not promise invoice == console to the token.” I’ve seen that happen.

If Product can confirm the cohort eligibility logic in plain English, I can add it to the quoting doc.

Isabelle

—
Isabelle Laurent
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference


From: Chris Osei <chris.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 11:22 AM PT
Subject: Re: Pricing guidance during Hosted API experiment — enablement materials + rollout plan

Agree we need to centralize.

Experiment status (high level):
- Active cohorts are self-serve + low-touch (no existing MSA / no custom rate card). Enterprise pipeline is excluded by default.
- Variants: adjusted free credits on signup + simplified overage tiers. No change to metering definitions (tokens/embeddings/rerank) — only the $ applied.
- Guardrails: any custom discount requires Sales Ops + Finance approval; we’re trying to measure price sensitivity, so ad hoc discounting inside the cohort breaks the readout.

Re: your questions:
- Stacking: my recommendation is “no stacking” for experiment cohorts (credits already act like a discount); for excluded enterprise deals it’s business-as-usual.
- Existing contract rate cards: keep them on contract; only apply experiment to net-new self-serve signups unless we explicitly move them for a reason (and we should log those).
- Console vs invoice: we should include the standard caveats + the runbook link for disputes. Wei/Finance can sanity check the wording.

Nikhil can confirm the eligibility rules with more precision.

Chris

—
Chris Osei
Product Ops (Pricing/Packaging), Redwood Inference


From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chris Osei <chris.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 12:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Pricing guidance during Hosted API experiment — enablement materials + rollout plan

Adding specifics on eligibility + what reps should say:

Eligibility (current config):
- Included: new self-serve accounts created after Jan 6, 2026; region = US or EU; spend < $25k trailing 90 days (obviously new accounts qualify).
- Excluded: any account flagged “Enterprise Assisted” in HubSpot OR with an executed contract rate card OR Dedicated/Private opportunities.

Quoting guidance:
- For included cohorts: do NOT apply additional discretionary discounts. If there’s a strategic reason, we can exempt them from experiment (move to standard pricing) but that’s a Product + Sales Ops call so we don’t poison the experiment.
- For excluded cohorts: standard quoting motions apply (enterprise pricing, commits, etc.).

Messaging (one liner):
“We’re running a limited-duration onboarding offer to simplify getting started; usage is still measured the same way (tokens/requests), but your included credits and overage tiers may differ based on signup date and plan.”

On console vs invoice: I’d keep it neutral and avoid getting deep on rounding mechanics in outbound comms. Internally we can include all the detail.

Nikhil

—
Nikhil Sharma
Product Lead, Hosted API Pricing
Redwood Inference


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: Finance review request: experiment quoting guidance + meter FAQ (for AEs/CSMs)

Laura (cc Emily),

We’re consolidating AE/CSM guidance for the active Hosted API experiment. Can you do a quick Finance review on the two things below?

1) Rule: “No stacking” (no additional discretionary discount) for included experiment cohorts, to preserve measurement integrity.
2) Metering FAQ language: our draft includes a short section on why console vs invoice might differ (time zone cutoffs, streaming partials, retries/failed requests not billed, rounding). We’ll link to the internal canonical meter definitions + dispute runbook.

Goal is to publish Monday and run training mid-week.

Attaching the updated drafts:
- Pricing_Metering_FAQ_for_AEs_CSMs_draft_v0.4.docx
- Experiment_Quote_Guidance_OnePager_v2.pdf

If you’re comfortable, I’ll note “Finance approved” in the Confluence page history and keep a copy of this email for audit trail.

Thanks,
Jordan


From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Chris Osei <chris.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 11:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Finance review request: experiment quoting guidance + meter FAQ (for AEs/CSMs)

Reviewed.

A few edits requested (mostly to reduce “we guarantee X” type statements):
- In the FAQ, change “invoice will always match console after month-end close” to “invoice is the billing source of truth; console is near-real-time reporting and may differ slightly due to timing/normalization.”
- Add a clear escalation path for discrepancies: Support ticket + required artifacts (invoice PDF, org_id, time window, example request_ids) + expected response time.
- Don’t mention specific variance thresholds in AE-facing content (keep that internal). If a customer asks, route to Finance/Support.

On #1 (no stacking for included cohorts): Finance supports, with the caveat that any exceptions need approval (Sales Ops + Finance) and should be logged.

Laura can confirm final approval, but from billing controls side I’m good once the language tweaks are in.

Emily

—
Emily Stone
Billing Controls & Close Support, Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Finance review request: experiment quoting guidance + meter FAQ (for AEs/CSMs)

Approved with Emily’s edits.

Two additional notes to incorporate:
- Please include a prominent line: “Meter definitions are documented here (internal), and any customer-facing commitments must reference the contract/order form.” We want to avoid reps paraphrasing metering mechanics inaccurately.
- For any customer asking about audits / dispute windows, route to Legal + Finance. Don’t improvise.

Once Wei updates the Confluence page, tag me and Emily on the final link.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
VP Finance (Exec Sponsor)
Redwood Inference
